answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost.
